title: Chicken or turkey and potatoes with gravy

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of roasted or braised chicken or turkey meat served with boiled or baked potatoes and a gravy made from meat broth, cream or flour. It is a traditional hearty meal popular at family lunches and holiday tables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey belong to the pheasant family, but their meat differs in flavor and fat content.
Traditionally the potatoes are cooked with the skin on to retain nutrients.
Gravy is often made from the pan drippings left after cooking the meat, enhancing the aroma.
Some regions add herbs (rosemary, thyme) or spices (paprika) to the gravy for extra flavor.
The dish can be adapted for dietary needs by using lean cuts or dairy‑free alternatives in the sauce.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium and magnesium, helping maintain normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared without excess oil, the dish is low in saturated fat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Serving potatoes with the skin adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to proteins in chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravy often contains salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: High glycemic index of potatoes
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, which can quickly raise blood sugar in diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the meat into portions and placing potatoes alongside. Pour gravy over the meat or serve it on the side. Fresh vegetables or herbs can be added for extra balance.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat thoroughly to a boil to destroy any bacteria. The dish can be frozen for up to 2 months, preferably divided into single servings.
